execution_context.trigger: runtime (client-side, during user checkout or form submission)
execution_context.file_location: injected third-party JavaScript on eCommerce checkout page

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses the credit card input field on the checkout page, reads its value, and sends the data via HTTP POST to a hardcoded external domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code directly collects sensitive credit card information from user input fields and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled server, which is a hallmark of web skimming attacks such as Magecart.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate third-party scripts on checkout pages should never access or transmit raw payment data to untrusted domains; only authorized payment processors should handle such data, and always to vetted, PCI-compliant endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may collect and transmit card data, but only to trusted, PCI-compliant endpoints and with explicit user consent. They do not send raw card numbers to unknown or unverified domains.
key_indicators: Direct access to payment input fields (e.g., credit card number)
Outbound HTTP POST requests to hardcoded, untrusted domains
Execution within the context of sensitive checkout or payment pages
Absence of user notification or consent for data transmission

attack_chain.action: Malicious third-party JavaScript is injected into the eCommerce site, often via a supply chain compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimming code in the user's browser during checkout.

attack_chain.action: The injected code executes in the browser, harvesting credit card and PII from form fields.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Stolen data is sent to an external server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives and monetizes stolen payment information.

behavioral_signatures: Client-side JavaScript accessing payment or PII input fields on checkout pages
Outbound HTTP POST requests from checkout pages to untrusted or unknown domains
Dynamic injection or modification of scripts from third-party or Nth-party sources
file_indicators: Unexpected or recently changed third-party JavaScript files on checkout pages
References to external scripts or domains not present in the original codebase
network_indicators: POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the merchant or payment processor (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/collect)
Unusual traffic patterns from checkout pages to new or suspicious endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript on sensitive pages that accesses payment or PII fields and initiates outbound network requests to untrusted domains. Enforce strict content security policies (CSP) to restrict script sources, and employ runtime monitoring to detect unauthorized data exfiltration. Regularly audit third-party and Nth-party scripts for unexpected changes, new external references, or behaviors involving sensitive data access and transmission.
